anchors.paper_title: Estimating endogenous changes in task performance from EEG
anchors.reason: The 2014 paper applies EEG performance estimation to baseline simulated driving and a perceptual discrimination task. The Mind Wandering dataset extends the Baseline Driving paradigm and is not this paper's data.

anchors.paper_title: Event-related alpha perturbations related to the scaling of steering wheel corrections
anchors.reason: Brooks & Kerick 2015 studies alpha ERSP and steering corrections in a driving task, topically related to BCIT driving data but not describing the Mind Wandering dataset itself.

anchors.paper_title: Estimating direction in brain-behavior interactions: Proactive and reactive brain states in driving
anchors.reason: Garcia et al. 2017 analyzes EEG-behavior directionality in driving, likely from BCIT driving data; it does not introduce the Mind Wandering dataset (audio and vigilance task).

anchors.paper_title: Automated EEG mega-analysis I: Spectral and amplitude characteristics across studies
anchors.reason: Multi-study EEG mega-analysis (18 studies) that likely includes BCIT data, but it is not this Mind Wandering dataset's data paper; it is a pooled analysis paper.

anchors.paper_title: Automated EEG mega-analysis II: Cognitive aspects of event related features
anchors.reason: Mega-analysis of 17 EEG studies using HED tags; may include BCIT data but is a multi-study analysis paper, not this dataset's data descriptor.

metadata.methods_description: Participants completed a practice session, then a 15-minute Calibration Driving task followed by three counter-balanced 30-minute Mind Wandering driving conditions (A: task-relevant audio, B: non-task-relevant audio, C: internal-focus audio) in a driving simulator. EEG was recorded with BioSemi 64(+8) channel systems with 4 eye and 2 mastoid channels at 2048 Hz, along with SMI REDEYE250 eye tracking and vehicle logs at 100 Hz. Participants responded to lateral perturbations and pressed a button on detecting police vehicles.
